description:
## Why
Elixir refuses a spec type variable that `when` does not declare ("type a/0 undefined") and a `var` used only once ("type variable a is used only once ... equivalent to term()"); fz accepts both, so lib specs and 01080 are not valid Elixir. Owner decision 2026-11-17: declare every variable, `v: var` when used two or more times, `v: term()` when used once.

## What changes
- `term` is a builtin type resolving to the same Ty as `any`, as in Erlang/Elixir (erl_internal is_type(term, 0); dialyzer erl_types from_form term -> t_any()).
- Every spec in lib/*.fz, fixtures and guides declares its type variables. On origin/develop 14470768a: 195 lib specs (257 `var`, 22 `term()`), 15 fixture specs (13 `var`, 6 `term()`).
- World::resolve_spec refuses, with a span and Elixir's wording, an undeclared type variable and a `var` used once.
- Fixture 01080: both specs declare `a`, the fixture is in Elixir form with `# oracle: self`, its twin is deleted.
- .agent/docs/specs.md states the rule.

## Measured
The lib rewrite with `any` in place of `term()` passes the whole workspace suite (6976 passed, 0 failed, no pin moved): a once-used variable bounded by term() is the unbounded variable fz already had.

## Signal
No undeclared or once-used `var` type variable in lib, fixtures or guides; a diagnostic fixture for each refusal; 01080 is its own oracle; full gate green.
title: A spec declares every type variable in when, as Elixir requires, and term is any
